name: Lean
note: dependent types; Lean 4 is also a general PL
typeSystem: Dependent types based on the Calculus of Constructions with inductive types, used both to state mathematical theorems as types and to construct proofs interactively via tactics.
runtime: The Lean 3 kernel and elaborator were implemented in C++ for performance, while user tactics and metaprograms were written and executed in Lean itself. External tools, including Python-based mathlib project tooling, managed packages and build workflows rather than tactic execution.

runtimes.name: Native (C++ kernel)
runtimes.role: Lean 3's small, trusted kernel and elaborator, implemented in C++ and compiled to native code.

compilers.name: lean (Lean 3)
compilers.role: Type-checks and elaborates Lean 3 theories and tactic proofs; superseded by the from-scratch Lean 4 compiler.

concurrencyModel: N/A as a user programming model in Lean 3. The editor server could perform background processing, but Lean 3 did not expose the general task-based concurrency model provided by Lean 4.

codeExample.caption: Lean 3: factorial defined by pattern matching and proved positive
codeExample.source:
def fact : ℕ → ℕ
| 0     := 1
| (n+1) := (n+1) * fact n

theorem fact_pos : ∀ n, fact n > 0 :=
begin
  intro n,
  induction n with n ih,
  { simp [fact] },
  { exact nat.mul_pos (nat.succ_pos n) ih }
end
